published_pet_friendly.method: Every published record carries PER-FIELD evidence entries (274 across 53 records), each with its own quote, source_url, artifact_sha256, capture_method and source_grade. Each record's composed evidence_quote carries fee, weight, count or species detail, which an amenity chip cannot express. Where this market owns the captured page, the operative label-value block was re-located in it.

findings.severity: evidence grade, not a live-output defect
findings.what: The published refusal quote 'Pets not allowed' is located in this market's OWN captured page at an amenity-list line, between 'Meeting rooms' and 'All Amenities'. The page's operative 'Hotel policies > Pets' panel is empty of content, which the founder note for this record already states.
findings.why_it_matters: Repository doctrine is that an amenity chip is never operative policy evidence. The FACT is probably right, since the amenity flag is first-party and property-specific, but the evidence does not meet the grade the other 16 no-pets records meet.
findings.live_output_effect: None. A VERIFIED_NO_PETS record suppresses a profile rather than publishing a policy, so no wrong pet policy is served.
findings.recommendation: Re-read the property's own Hotel Policies pet panel on a free attended visit and re-bind the quote. Do not flip the fact on this finding alone.

parallelism_safety.shared_file_justification: This is the unavoidable bookkeeping registration the order permits. `data/acquisition/` is shared by every market, and its classification gate fails on any run directory nobody has decided about. TWO Pittsburgh run ids were APPENDED to OTHER_MARKET_RUNS. No existing entry was edited, reordered or removed, and no Milwaukee classification changed.
parallelism_safety.merge_note: Indianapolis is running concurrently in a separate worktree and may append its OWN run ids to this same set. That is an ADDITIVE conflict. The correct resolution is to preserve BOTH sets of entries -- every Pittsburgh id and every Indianapolis id -- never to take one side. Dropping either market's entries re-opens the classification gate for that market.
